text: Refining D-0206 after #355's review: a backing test's calls count only where the test method made them, directly or through code it called, never through unittest's or the runner's own code except where unittest calls a callable the test handed an assertion, as assertRaises(E, f, x) does, so setUp, tearDown and an assertion's own work count nothing. A call matches by identity, the very code object or C callable resolved, and only an application declaration, compiled anew from its staged source, matches by equal code. A class resolves to the methods compiled in its own body, by their code's qualified name, and each counts only when called on the class, an instance or a subclass; a C method descriptor counts only where the receiver's type resolves its name to it. The runner refuses up front what it can't observe, so its contract stays untested: a class with no method of its own, such as a type written in C or a dataclass whose methods are all generated, slot wrappers, method-wrappers and C special methods, which syntax reaches, and a standard-library module sys.stdlib_module_names doesn't list. The file reported and checked against a RECORD is the one the counted code is in, or a C function's extension. A backing test that runs twice in one invocation fails its evidence with a diagnostic instead of the attribution. A binding problem is named before missing calls, each backing test's record carries boundary_calls and assertions and each implementation recorded, zeros included, and the gate's build step and the direct route mark each backing-test run alike, passing only where its row is tested.
